en.html:
We were taking nodate.

The plaster wall was keeping the winter wind out. Overhead, the sun had reached noon and was giving its warmth quite generously. The Nagakura garden could still make room for such refinement, season or no season.

I received the plain, rugged Bizen bowl in both hands. At the bottom lay a little tea, hot enough to make its presence known through the pottery.

en.html:
If black was what remained after shutting everything out, then it was abstinence.
If black was what remained after drinking everything in, it was vulgar indulgence.

...I see. The difference was in how one looked.

I lowered my eyes to the bowl in my hands. The brown pottery, almost black, enclosed the properly frothed matcha.

Between the two interpretations, I had to admit this view was doing more for Lady Kanae's case.

en.html:
Kageaki"...Captain. About Silver Star. Is that information beyond doubt?"
Kanae"Yes, so it would appear. Silver Star does seem to have made an appearance."
Kanae"At Fudaraku Castle. When that bomb was dropped."
Kageaki"...And then..."
Kanae"For some reason the bomb—though perhaps one ought not expect too much of a new weapon—failed to break the entire fortress. It left about half of it standing. Even so, they say the ground at the center was turned to desert."
Kanae"Silver Star was just—"
Kageaki"At that... center?"
Kanae"...That much I cannot establish. Only, for all the people who survived Fudaraku, there is not one who claims to have seen Silver Star, or any trace of it, after the blast."
Kageaki"————"

en.html:
Kageaki"For the Sasagawa Kubo, should this not be the occasion to try every available means of making peace? Even if the final break cannot be avoided, time gained is still a gain."
Kageaki"He must be ready to pay any price for the time to reorganize his army."
Kanae"Normally, yes. But that man does not oblige us by being normal."
Kanae"This morning, plans were announced for the engagement of His Highness Kuniuji and the present head of the Ootori house—Hanae."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"Of course, Shishiku is arranging to take all authority in Rokuhara into his own hands. Once he belongs to the shogun's wife's family, who will find it strange that he should run the shogunate?"
Kanae"When a man is in such a hurry to secure power, is it not because he is in an equal hurry to use it? What do you say?"
Kageaki"Which leaves only a decisive battle with the occupation forces. ...I see."
Kanae"Nothing will open up by shutting ourselves away in Aizu. Put everything on the one battle and let it decide our fortune."
Kanae"Something on those lines, I imagine."
Kageaki"But Captain, even on those lines, surely there are more pressing matters? To make himself the shogunal family's relative before anything else—I am unable to see the necessity."
Kageaki"Call it what it is: a formality. With the Sasagawa army already under his command, he should have no need to give it such importance."
Kanae"And there you have Shishiku. He must have his formality."
Kageaki"..."
Kanae"Form, the proper course, the proper reason. That is the whole man."
Kanae"A formalist through to his marrow."
Kageaki"...But Captain. Such a man, in—"

Kanae"Moriuji Ashikaga is already dead. The Kubo of Koga, Oyumi and Horigoe are probably under Fudaraku's soil by now. Once Shishiku too is gone, there is no keeping Rokuhara from collapse."
Kageaki"There will be nobody left with the ability to lead it."
Kanae"Yes."
Kageaki"But Captain, will all this not amount to doing GHQ's work for it?"
Kanae"The occupation army comes marching into a leaderless Aizu?"
Kageaki"Yes. —No. I see."
Kageaki"There would be nothing to attack for..."
Kanae"That is how it works out, no? Without Shishiku, Rokuhara will destroy itself. We need not put the occupation army to the trouble."
Kanae"Make an unnecessary war, and on what grounds do you expect the people of Yamato to trust you?"
Kageaki"GHQ will have to reconsider its whole strategy for ruling Yamato. ...Though with Yamato's own military force gone, that should not prove especially difficult."
Kanae"True. But perhaps we may expect some resourcefulness from the gentleman we spared?"
Kanae"Enough to take charge of a Rokuhara army with its head removed, at least. If he cannot manage even that and only keeps himself shut away, what use have we preserved him for? Really."
Kageaki"...I imagine the gentleman may have his own explanation."
Kanae"Shall I put the question to him?"

en.html: Of the plan, she meant. Naturally. Kill Shishiku Ootori, the Sasagawa Kubo. Bring Rokuhara to collapse from within. Frustrate GHQ's designs. As an operation, it was effective. Assassinate him successfully, and in all probability the decisive battle between Rokuhara and the occupation forces would never begin. A restored shogunate. Rule by GHQ. For many people in Yamato, both were unwelcome futures; both would be pushed further away. Whatever came afterwards, for the immediate present that much was possible. Effective. I could not refuse to admit it.◆ But this was terrorism. A challenge to the power of words. The same thing we had already done in attacking the airship, one could say. Yes. But the target there had been a bomb. An inanimate object, to the last. This time, a human being. One person's life taken for a political end. However right that end, it supplied no absolution. Shishiku Ootori too was surely doing what he believed to be right. Did I accept a political argument made by violence, or did I not?
en.text:
Of the plan, she meant. Naturally.

Kill Shishiku Ootori, the Sasagawa Kubo. Bring Rokuhara to collapse from within. Frustrate GHQ's designs.

As an operation, it was effective. Assassinate him successfully, and in all probability the decisive battle between Rokuhara and the occupation forces would never begin.

A restored shogunate. Rule by GHQ. For many people in Yamato, both were unwelcome futures; both would be pushed further away. Whatever came afterwards, for the immediate present that much was possible.

Effective. I could not refuse to admit it.◆

But this was terrorism.

A challenge to the power of words.

The same thing we had already done in attacking the airship, one could say. Yes. But the target there had been a bomb. An inanimate object, to the last.

This time, a human being.
One person's life taken for a political end.

However right that end, it supplied no absolution. Shishiku Ootori too was surely doing what he believed to be right.

Did I accept a political argument made by violence, or did I not?

ja.html: このプランを、という意味だろう。無論。 　――篠川公方大鳥獅子吼を殺害し、六波羅を自壊へ 導き、ＧＨＱの企図を挫く。 　作戦効果は認められる。 　暗殺に成功すれば、六波羅と進駐軍の決戦は未発に 終わる見込みが濃い。 　幕府の再興とＧＨＱの支配、多くの大和国民にとっ て望ましからざる未来は二つ共に遠ざかる。 　後々のことはともかく、ひとまずのところは。 　有効だ。認めざるを得ない。◆ 　しかし、これは、暴力主義テロリズムである。 　言論の力に対する挑戦である。 　既に為した、飛行艦襲撃と同じ事と言えばそうだ。 　が、あれはあくまで爆弾という無機物を標的にした 行動だった。 　今度は人間。 　政治目的の為に、一個人の生命を奪う。 　その目的がいかに正しかろうと、免罪符の役は果た さない。 　大鳥獅子吼とて、正しいと信じた行いをしている事 に変わりはなかろうからだ。 　暴力による政治主張を、肯んずるか否か。
ja.text:
このプランを、という意味だろう。無論。

　――篠川公方大鳥獅子吼を殺害し、六波羅を自壊へ
導き、ＧＨＱの企図を挫く。

　作戦効果は認められる。
　暗殺に成功すれば、六波羅と進駐軍の決戦は未発に
終わる見込みが濃い。

　幕府の再興とＧＨＱの支配、多くの大和国民にとっ
て望ましからざる未来は二つ共に遠ざかる。
　後々のことはともかく、ひとまずのところは。

　有効だ。認めざるを得ない。◆


　しかし、これは、暴力主義テロリズムである。

　言論の力に対する挑戦である。

　既に為した、飛行艦襲撃と同じ事と言えばそうだ。
　が、あれはあくまで爆弾という無機物を標的にした
行動だった。

　今度は人間。
　政治目的の為に、一個人の生命を奪う。

　その目的がいかに正しかろうと、免罪符の役は果た
さない。
　大鳥獅子吼とて、正しいと信じた行いをしている事
に変わりはなかろうからだ。

　暴力による政治主張を、肯んずるか否か。
